headline: High risk of data leakage and cascading errors: Firecrawl’s broad egress can expose sensitive web/API-key context to RD-Agent’s external LLM APIs, while shared multi-instance workflows raise conflict and prompt-injection exposure.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Firecrawl ingests web content and exposes MCP-compatible/API outputs; RD-Agent consumes LLM-driven research workflows and can run browsers. A shared filesystem or manual handoff is not documented, so direct injection is not proven, but Firecrawl’s raw content can become RD-Agent input if bridged. Uncertainty keeps this at medium rather than low.
conditions: IF Firecrawl output is copied into RD-Agent prompts or files without sanitization, injected instructions can steer downstream actions.
IF an MCP or file bridge is added between the agents, attacker-controlled web text can traverse the boundary.
mitigations: Strip instructions from scraped text before passing it onward.
Use a fixed schema for Firecrawl outputs and reject free-form text.
Disable any automatic copy/paste or file handoff between agents.
Add a human review step for pages containing prompts or code blocks.
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to all transferred content.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Firecrawl touches API keys and broad web content, and RD-Agent sends data to third-party LLM APIs by default. Even without a documented shared workspace, any handoff of Firecrawl outputs into RD-Agent can leak sensitive content off-box. Because both agents have broad egress and the pairwise bridge is plausible, the safer severity is high.
conditions: IF Firecrawl outputs include API keys, screenshots, or structured data and are forwarded to RD-Agent, those contents can be transmitted to external model APIs.
IF both agents are run under the same workspace or OAuth principal, cross-agent exposure of sensitive files becomes possible.
mitigations: Do not pass secrets-bearing Firecrawl outputs into RD-Agent.
Redact API keys and screenshots before any transfer.
Run the agents in separate workspaces with separate credentials.
Turn off network egress for one side during sensitive runs.
requires-engineering: enforce DLP filters on all inter-agent transfers.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents support multiple instances and both have broad network egress; Firecrawl also has API/CLI surfaces while RD-Agent uses APIs and Docker isolation. There is no documented shared lock or shared mutable resource, so a direct write-write conflict is not established. Still, concurrent runs can contend over shared files, logs, or external quotas if co-located.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same directory or log path, concurrent writes can collide.
IF both agents share the same external API quota or credential set, one agent can starve the other.
mitigations: Assign separate working directories.
Use separate API keys per agent.
Serialize writes to any shared log or artifact path.
Monitor quota usage during parallel runs.
requires-engineering: add file locks or a job scheduler.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Firecrawl produces extracted web content and RD-Agent is a research automation system with browser and LLM-backed workflows. If RD-Agent treats Firecrawl output as authoritative, errors or poisoned content can cascade into generated reports, code, or actions. No verification gate is documented, so the default pathway is risky enough for high severity.
conditions: IF RD-Agent consumes Firecrawl output without source verification, hallucinations or poisoned pages can propagate into downstream artifacts.
IF RD-Agent is configured to act on generated findings, incorrect upstream content can trigger incorrect actions.
mitigations: Require citation checks before RD-Agent uses Firecrawl output.
Compare extracted claims against the original page or a second source.
Limit RD-Agent to read-only analysis for Firecrawl-fed tasks.
Flag low-confidence extractions for manual review.
requires-engineering: add automated verification against source URLs.

E_compliance.rationale: Firecrawl handles web content and API keys, while RD-Agent touches financial reports, competition datasets, logs, and research papers and sends data to external model APIs. The profiles do not document residency or retention controls, so a compliance mismatch is plausible but not proven. Uncertainty keeps this at medium rather than low.
conditions: IF regulated or personal data is included in Firecrawl outputs and then processed by RD-Agent’s external APIs, residency or retention obligations may be violated.
IF the operator requires strict log retention limits, RD-Agent’s log files can retain sensitive material.
mitigations: Exclude regulated data from both agents.
Review retention settings for logs and artifacts.
Use region-appropriate API endpoints where available.
Delete temporary files after each run.
requires-engineering: document a data-processing agreement and residency policy.
